llm.summary: This skill is a local nginx configuration linter that reads user-selected config files and reports issues without network use, persistence, or hidden mutation.

dimensions.detail: Local file reads of nginx config paths are proportionate for a config linter, and inspection found no network calls, credential-store access, shell execution, or data upload behavior.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package manager step, remote retrieval, or dependency installation is present; the artifact is a Markdown skill plus a local Python stdlib script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The commands read a user-provided file or recursively scan nginx config directories; this is purpose-aligned, but users should avoid pointing it at broad private directories because it will read matching config files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not create services, scheduled tasks, hooks, background workers, memory entries, privilege escalation paths, or persistent state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is linting and auditing nginx configuration files, and the bundled Python script implements parsing, syntax checks, security checks, performance checks, and report formatting for that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the skill read nginx configuration files you explicitly pass to it. Treat reports as local diagnostic output, and avoid using recursive mode on directories that contain unrelated private configs.
llm.findings: [LP3] expected: The scanner concern about local file reads is supported, but those reads are the core function of a nginx config linter and are user-directed. I did not find artifact-backed network-capable behavior or hidden overbroad access beyond reading supplied files or .conf files in a supplied directory.
